newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's 1997 GDP to stay flat, inflation 11 pct.
newsitem.headline: Russia's 1997 GDP to stay flat, inflation 11 pct.

text.p: Russia's 1997 gross domestic product is likely to be unchanged on 1996 levels and annual inflation will fall to 11 percent from 22 percent, a senior government official said on Thursday.

State Statistics Committee First Deputy Chairman Valery Dalin told a news conference that by the committee's estimates 1997 industrial production volume would be unchanged or one percent higher than 1996 levels and GDP would be unchanged.
He said annual inflation would amount to 11 percent. The 1997 budget foresees a 12 percent inflation rate.
The government, which until recently had been forecasting growth of up to two percent this year, now concedes that the economy will not grow significantly until 1998.
Dalin said the situation in the first four months of 1997 was stable.
"Stabilisation and depression are one word for the same phenomenon," Dalin said. "But stabilisation has a more optimistic feel."

In the first four months of 1997 GDP was unchanged year-on-year. Dalin said industrial production, trade and transportation volumes rose by 0.5 to one percent, while agricultural production fell by six percent and construction volumes fell by four percent year-on-year.
Investment fell by eight percent, he said.
Dalin said tax arrears had fallen to over 60 trillion roubles by the end of April from 118.8 trillion roubles at the start of December, 1996.
Dalin said the committee had changed its estimate for the share of the shadow economy in GDP to 25 percent from 22 percent, but said changes had not had a material impact on the GDP figures.
Earlier this year the committee reported modest year-on-year growth rates in GDP, which economists said was partly due to the shadow economy estimate revision.
